title: Lesson 44 - We Need a Better Option

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: The rehearsal showed that our small direction card isn't clear enough. We need a better option before the public event.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Let's compare the three ideas by the same criteria: clarity, accessibility, cost, storage and staffing.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Option one is a set of printed wall arrows that lead from the front doors to the side gallery. They cost about forty-five dollars.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: The advantage is a continuous route. The downside is that adhesive has to be approved, and the arrows are mostly single-use.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Option two is two reusable standing signs: one next to the service desk and one that faces people leaving the elevator. The quote is one hundred eighty dollars, including one sample panel.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: They can be moved, stored and used for later events. We'd have the large text printed on replaceable panels.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Option three is a volunteer greeter who stays near the front doors.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: A person can answer questions, but one greeter won't cover the whole afternoon. We'd need two volunteers per hour and a backup for breaks.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: The main trade-off is flexibility versus dependable coverage.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: What would you do?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: If I were you, I'd choose the standing signs as the base plan. The safest option is the one that doesn't depend on continuous staffing or wall adhesive.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I agree, but let's keep one greeter for the opening hour, when questions will be most frequent.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Based on our criteria, the best fit is two standing signs plus one opening-hour greeter. The signs stay within the two-hundred-dollar wayfinding limit.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: We should still test readability. I'm having one sample panel printed before the full order.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: And the payment record should be checked before anything is reordered. We were charged twice last time, even though the refund has now been issued.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Good. I'll ask for one itemized quote and written approval before the full order is placed.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: The downside is storage. Where will the signs go afterward?

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: In the closet that is behind the service desk. Facilities confirmed that the lower shelf is available.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Then we can revisit the layout if the sample is hard to read, but we don't need to reopen the whole decision.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Agreed. I'll send a summary with the option, reasons, cost limit, sample test and owners.
